newsitem.title: USA: Top "Afrocentrism" scholar to leave post amid probe.
newsitem.headline: Top "Afrocentrism" scholar to leave post amid probe.

text.p: A founder of the "Afrocentrism" academic movement who is the target of a plagiarism investigation will step down from his post as chairman of Temple University's African American studies department, a Temple spokeswoman said Thursday.
Professor Molefi Asante "will be stepping down sometime between now and the end of the academic year," spokeswoman Harriet Goodheart said.

She said the decision was announced Wednesday evening by the dean of Temple's College of Arts and Sciences, and was ndependent of a misconduct investigation into accusations Asante plagiarised a colleague's work, charges Asante has denied.

Asante is regarded as a pioneer in the Afrocentrism movement, which seeks to teach world history from an African perspective, in part to bolster black self-esteem and political unity. Some Afrocentrist theories have sparked controversies over whether they exaggerate contributions of African cultures.
Asante will remain a faculty member at Temple, Goodheart said. A national search will be conducted for his successor as chairman of the department.

The probe at Temple focuses on charges by an assistant in Asante's department that he improperly appropriated her work in a high school text book, "African-American History: A Journal of Liberation," that he authored.
Goodheart said that investigation is still under way.
Asante has said the allegations were the result of a poor performance review of the assistant.
